question.problem: An arithmetic sequence has the $3$rd term ${a}_{3}=-9$ and the $8$th term ${a}_{8}=-19.$  Calculate the $11$th term.
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by 

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

 

so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

To find the common difference, we can find the total difference between the terms ${a}_{3}=-9$ and ${a}_{8}=-19$ and divide it by the number of jumps, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\frac{{a}_{8}-{a}_{3}}{8-3} \\  & =\frac{-19-(-9)}{8-3} \\  & =\frac{-10}{5} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{3}=-9,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{3}$ is $2$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{3} & ={a}_{1}+2d \\ -9 & ={a}_{1}+2(-2) \\ -9 & ={a}_{1}-4 \\ {a}_{1} & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-5+(n-1)\cdot (-2) \\  & =-5-2n+2 \\  & =-3-2n\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can find the $11$th term by substituting $n=11$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{11} & =-3-2(11) \\  & =-3-22 \\  & =-25\end{aligned}
$$
